thread.title: Close Update: S&P 500, Nasdaq Snap 3-Day Win Streak on Consumer and Tech Losses

title: Close Update: S&P 500, Nasdaq Snap 3-Day Win Streak on Consumer and Tech Losses
text:
Close Update: S&P 500, Nasdaq Snap 3-Day Win Streak on Consumer and Tech Losses April 19, 2018, 04:23:57 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
U.S. stocks were weaker Thursday, off the day's lows by the bell but still in the red as the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite stemmed three-day winning streaks while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell for a second consecutive session. 
Losses were spread through much of the S&P, with consumer staples skidding 3.1% as cigarette company Philip Morris ( PM ) posted a quarterly miss in revenue. The Nasdaq was held down with declines in semiconductor stocks that dented information technology. 
Financials posted a 1.5% gain as American Express ( AXP ) beat analysts' expectations with its results and posted the best advance on the S&P. Bank of New York Mellon's ( BK ) beat also aided the sector after the custodian bank topped expectations with its first quarter report. 
Stocks had started the week off on a winning note amid optimism heading into the first-quarter earnings season, but a number of downbeat results dampened sentiment. Treasury yields rose, with the 10-year touching above 2.9%. 
"Today's technical weakness comes from modestly overbought conditions on a short-term basis, coupled with rallying yields," Janney's Dan Wantrobski said in a trading note. Investors may "look to de-risk as the 10-year approaches (and possibly surpasses) that 3% barrier." 
Apple ( AAPL ) retreated in one of the Dow's worst losses, sending the S&P's tech group down 1.1%. That was after supplier Taiwan Semiconductor's ( TSM ) revenue guidance disappointed in its quarterly earnings. NVIDIA (NVDA) fell 3.1%, Micron (MU) shed 4.8% and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was down 2.4%.
